guideTitle: 6 Best Grab Bars With Paper Holders in 2026
metaTitle: Best Grab Bars With Paper Holders 2026
metaDescription: Six grab bars with built-in toilet paper holders compared by length, roll capacity, capacity rating and finish, for compact bathrooms.
introParagraphs: A grab bar with a built-in toilet paper holder solves a small, common problem: the wall beside the toilet is the one place you want both a handhold and a roll within easy reach, and there is rarely room for two separate fixtures. Combining them puts support exactly where a hand already goes.

This lineup includes the Moen 8-inch bar with a holder, the Delta Brilliance stainless bar with a pivoting holder rated to 300 lb, the Healthcraft 14.3-inch bar with a 9-hole flange and three longer two-roll bars from FANHAO at 18 inches and Zepolu and iHansee at 17 inches. Stated capacities run from 250 lb on the Moen to 300 lb on the Delta.

We evaluated each pick on bar length, tube diameter, how many rolls it holds, finish and the way the holder is built, since a holder that is awkward to reload defeats the point. As always, the wall behind the bar sets the real limit, so each one needs studs or solid backing.

products.name: Delta Brilliance Stainless Grab Bar With Paper Holder, 41550-SS
products.description:
Delta's combination bar is built from a stainless steel assist bar on zinc posts, and the listing says the built-in assist bar supports up to 300 lb while providing stability and leverage within a practical bathroom accessory. The holder pivots, which makes reloading a roll a simple motion instead of a fiddly one. It is a mainstream, brand-backed way to add support beside the toilet.

The pivoting holder is the feature to appreciate. It means you can swing it aside to change the roll, and it means the bar and the holder are one coordinated piece, so the paper hangs in a predictable place for a hand that might reach without looking. Stud mounting is the intended path, and the 300 lb rating assumes it.

Compared with the Moen 8-inch bar it states a higher capacity, and compared with the longer two-roll bars it is simpler and more compact. It is the pick for a household that wants a recognizable brand and a tidy look that blends with a stainless fixture set.

products.name: Moen Brushed Nickel 8 Inch Grab Bar With Paper Holder
products.description:
Moen's LR2352 line gives you an 8-inch stainless steel bar with an integrated toilet paper holder in a lightly brushed warm-gray nickel finish. The listing says it supports up to 250 lb and that it screws into the stud and mounts to the bathroom wall. A companion chrome version lists a 1-inch bar diameter, which suggests the slim profile of this line.

Eight inches is very short, so think of this as a steadying handle, not a rail. It is best suited to the person who needs a small point of contact while sitting down or rising, not someone who relies on sliding a hand along a bar. The slim tube may not suit stiff fingers.

Compared with the Delta, it lists a lower capacity and a shorter bar, though its Moen styling is more discreet. Compared with the Healthcraft at 14.3 inches it is smaller and simpler. It fits a compact bathroom with brushed nickel fixtures where the main aim is a clean look and a light handhold.
products.bestFor: A discreet nickel handle in a compact bathroom.
cons: 8 in length gives a single grab point
Slim tube may not suit stiff fingers

products.name: FANHAO 18 Inch Matte Black Grab Bar With Double Paper Holder
products.description:
FANHAO pairs an 18-inch matte black bar with a double toilet paper roll holder, in 304 stainless steel with a knurled surface the listing says gives reliable non-slip support even when wet. The pitch is a two-in-one, space-saving unit. A second roll in the holder means you reload less often.

A longer bar gives more grip positions than the 8-inch Moen, and the knurling helps when hands are damp. The black finish suits a modern bathroom but will show scratches over time, and any combined unit means that if the holder part breaks, the whole piece may need replacing.

Compared with the Zepolu and iHansee bars, which are 17 inches in brushed nickel, this one is slightly longer and in black. It is a good pick for a bathroom with black fixtures where the person using it wants more bar and a spare roll within reach. It is worth checking the listing photos for how far the double holder sits from the wall before you commit.

pros: 18 in bar gives more hand positions
cons: Black finish can scratch over time

products.name: Zepolu Brushed Nickel 17 Inch Grab Bar With Paper Roll Holder
products.description:
Zepolu offers a 17-inch brushed nickel bar with a 1.25-inch diameter, made from 304 stainless steel with a built-in holder that takes two rolls. The listing says it is resistant to rust, corrosion and tarnish, and that it is great for people who need a little help getting up from the toilet. The 1.25-inch tube is a comfortable hand size for many people.

The brushed nickel finish hides water spots better than chrome and matches nickel faucets. Holding two rolls gives the household an easy backup. It is a straightforward design with fewer special features than some competitors.

Compared with the FANHAO it is a little shorter and in nickel, and compared with the iHansee it is nearly identical in size and finish, so the choice can come down to the stated details. Compared with the Moen 8-inch bar it gives a more useful gripping length. It suits a bathroom where a mid-length, nickel-finished bar with a spare roll is wanted.
products.bestFor: A nickel bathroom wanting a mid-length bar and a spare roll.
cons: No capacity figure in the text we have
Brushed nickel shows fewer spots but not none

products.name: iHansee Brushed Nickel 17 Inch Grab Bar With Double Roll Holder
products.description:
iHansee's bar is a 17-inch brushed nickel unit in 304 stainless steel that combines support with a holder for two rolls. The listing says it suits settings from private homes to public restrooms in commercial buildings, hospitals and senior care facilities, so it is built with institutional use in mind. The brand also sells towel-rack versions.

That range of settings suggests a sturdy, plain design rather than a styled one. The double holder adds convenience and the nickel finish is easy to live with. As with all combined bars, check that the mounting plate aligns with studs and that the roll holder does not block a hand.

Compared with the Zepolu it is close in size and finish, so look at the details on the product page. Compared with the Healthcraft it offers more length but fewer design extras. It is a good fit for a family bathroom, rental or small facility that wants a practical nickel bar with two rolls.
products.bestFor: Rentals and shared bathrooms that want a plain two-roll bar.
pros: Used in homes and commercial settings
cons: No capacity figure in the text we have

products.name: Healthcraft Plus 14.3 Inch Paper Holder and Grab Bar, Brushed
products.description:
Healthcraft's Plus series combines a safety bar with a designer toilet paper holder in brushed stainless, using premium number 304 stainless steel with concealed screws. The standout feature is the 9-hole flange, which the listing says helps align the mount with wall studs and gives a stable install. At 14.3 inches it sits between the short Moen and the 17-inch bars.

A flange with nine holes is a real help in a retrofit, because it multiplies the chances that screws will land in framing when studs do not line up. The concealed screw covers give a clean face. The design is aimed at buyers who want the bar to look like part of the bathroom.

Compared with the Delta it is a more design-led piece, and compared with the Zepolu and iHansee it offers a smaller size but a better mounting system. It is the pick for a bathroom where the install is the uncertain part and a clean look matters.
products.bestFor: Retrofit installs where stud alignment is the worry.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A combination bar is two products in one, and the paper holder is part of the structure. The Delta lists up to 300 lb and the Moen 8-inch lists up to 250 lb, but a pivoting or integrated holder can change how the bar behaves under load. Treat these as helpful hand supports beside the toilet and confirm the stated capacity matches the way you will use it. For heavy support, a dedicated bar is often the stronger choice.

Some bars hold a single roll, like the Delta pivoting holder in the text we have, while the FANHAO, Zepolu and iHansee bars hold two. Two rolls mean fewer trips to change paper, which helps anyone for whom bending is a chore. Check that the holder opens easily and that a full roll sits clear of the wall and your hand. A bar that lets you reload a roll with one hand and without twisting is the better daily choice, even if it looks plainer.

Lengths run from 8 inches on the Moen to 18 inches on the FANHAO. A longer bar gives more hand positions, which matters when rising from a seat, while a short one is only a touch point. Tube diameter matters too: the Zepolu lists 1.25 inches and the Moen chrome sibling lists 1 inch. Choose a size you can wrap your hand around.

The Healthcraft 9-hole flange is built to align with studs, and the Moen mounts into a stud. Toilet walls often have plumbing and odd stud spacing, so a flexible flange helps. Locate studs before you buy, and confirm you can mount at a comfortable height. A bar mounted into drywall alone is not a safe plan.

Brushed nickel on the Moen, Zepolu and iHansee hides water spots better than chrome. Matte black on the FANHAO matches modern fixtures but can scratch. Delta's Brilliance stainless sits between the two. Pick the finish that suits the rest of the room and your cleaning habits.

A combined unit means a broken holder can mean a replaced bar. Check the warranty and whether parts are available. A simpler fixture like the Delta from a major brand is easier to replace than a lesser-known design. Think about how long you plan to keep the bathroom as it is.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity wording
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the stated capacities, 250 lb on the Moen and 300 lb on the Delta, and noted which listings gave none. Numbers were treated as installation-dependent, and holder designs were considered for how they affect the load path. Honest wording scored higher than bold claims. Reloading with one hand was a specific test case, because that is how most people actually change a roll.

howWeEvaluated.title: Holder usability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared one-roll and two-roll holders and the Delta pivot design. We asked whether reloading would be easy with one hand and whether the roll would clear the user. Holders that look awkward to reload were marked down. Where a listing gave no capacity, we left the figure blank and asked buyers to confirm it on the product page.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bar length and diameter
howWeEvaluated.description: Lengths from 8 to 18 inches and the 1.25-inch Zepolu tube were compared. The Healthcraft at 14.3 inches fit between the extremes. We considered how each size would serve a person rising from a toilet. Tube diameter was judged against the common 1.25 inch comfort range for adult hands.

howWeEvaluated.title: Install friendliness
howWeEvaluated.description: Flange design and mounting notes were compared, including the Healthcraft 9-hole flange and the Moen stud mount. We favored designs that help find studs. Concealed screw covers earned credit for appearance. A flange that tells you how to align with studs was treated as a practical safety feature.

howWeEvaluated.title: Finish and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: Brushed nickel, matte black, brushed stainless and Delta Brilliance finishes were compared for how they would look and clean. We noted which would show spots or scratches. Finish was weighted as a daily-life factor. We also asked how each finish would look after a year of daily wiping, not just when it arrives.

faq.q: Can a grab bar with a paper holder support my weight?
faq.a: It depends on the model and the install. The Delta lists up to 300 lb and the Moen 8-inch lists up to 250 lb when mounted into studs. A combined bar is best treated as a steadying aid, and if you need strong support a dedicated bar is the safer choice. If you are unsure about height, sit on the toilet and have someone hold a tape measure level with where your hand rests naturally, then mark that point.

faq.q: Where should the bar go next to the toilet?
faq.a: On the side wall at a height that lets your hand land naturally when you rise, usually around waist height. Check that the roll will not catch your elbow. Mark the position with tape and test the motion before drilling. Check how many rolls the holder takes before you decide, because the reloading routine is the part you will repeat every week.

faq.q: How do I choose between a one-roll and a two-roll model?
faq.a: A single-roll bar like the Delta is tidier, while a two-roll bar like the Zepolu or iHansee gives a built-in spare. If reloading is a chore, pick two rolls. If you prefer a minimalist look, pick one. A plumber or handyperson can find studs behind a toilet wall quickly if the area has pipes, and it is worth the small fee to avoid drilling into a line.

faq.q: Will it fit if the studs are in the wrong place?
faq.a: A flange with many holes, such as the Healthcraft 9-hole design, gives you more chances to hit framing. If that still fails, use rated wall anchors or add wood blocking behind the wall. Do not mount into drywall alone. If a holder part cracks, a manufacturer with a published warranty is more likely to send a replacement than a seller without one.

faq.q: Is a combined unit harder to repair?
faq.a: Yes, because a broken holder can mean replacing the whole bar. A major brand like Delta or Moen generally makes replacement easier. Check warranty terms before buying. Where the studs are far from the ideal bar position, a short length of wood blocking behind the wall during a renovation is a lasting fix.

faq.q: Does finish matter for a toilet bar?
faq.a: Mostly for looks and cleaning. Brushed nickel hides spots, matte black can scratch and stainless is a neutral middle. Choose the finish that matches your fixtures and wipe it regularly. If the bar will see heavy daily use, buy the model with the clearest capacity statement and mount it into studs with every screw supplied.
